arxiv-1910-03351.title: A Tracer-Based Algorithm for Automatic Generation of Seafloor Age Grids from Plate Tectonic Reconstructions
arxiv-1910-03351.creator: Krister S. Karlsen ( k.s.karlsen@geo.uio.no ), Mathew Domeier
arxiv-1910-03351.description: Abstract Abstract The age of the ocean floor and its time-dependent age distribution control fundamental features of the Earth, such as bathymetry, sea level and mantle heat loss. Recently, the development of increasingly sophisticated reconstructions of past plate motions has provided models for plate kinematics and plate boundary evolution back in geological time.

arxiv-2103-11515.title: A curated dataset for data-driven turbulence modelling
arxiv-2103-11515.creator: Ryley McConkey, Eugene Yee, Fue-Sang Lien
arxiv-2103-11515.description: Abstract The recent surge in machine learning augmented turbulence modelling is a promising approach for addressing the limitations of Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) models. This work presents the development of the first open-source dataset, curated and structured for immediate use in machine learning augmented turbulence closure modelling.

arxiv-2212-09788.title: Waves in the Lower Solar Atmosphere
arxiv-2212-09788.creator: David B. Jess 1, 2], Shahin Jafarzadeh 3, 4], Peter H. Keys 1, Marco Stangalini 5, Gary Verth 6, Samuel D. T. Grant 1
arxiv-2212-09788.description: Abstract Waves and oscillations have been observed in the Sun’s atmosphere for over half a century. While such phenomena have readily been observed across the entire electromagnetic spectrum, spanning radio to gamma-ray sources, the underlying role of waves in the supply of energy to the outermost extremities of the Sun’s corona has yet to be uncovered.

arxiv-2308-15734.title: Efficient and Explainable Graph Neural Architecture Search via Monte-Carlo Tree Search
arxiv-2308-15734.creator: Yuya Sasaki
arxiv-2308-15734.description: Abstract . Graph neural networks (GNNs) are powerful tools for performing data science tasks in various domains. Although we use GNNs in wide application scenarios, it is a laborious task for researchers and practitioners to design/select optimal GNN architectures in diverse graphs.

arxiv-2501-00591.creator: H. Cein Mandujano, Peter Y. Zavalij, Alicia Manjón-Sanz, Huibo Cao, Efrain E. Rodriguez
arxiv-2501-00591.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by H. Cein Mandujano, Peter Y. Zavalij, Alicia Manjón-Sanz, Huibo Cao, Efrain E. Rodriguez. In Co x NbSe 2 , crystal symmetry, and cobalt site occupation drive the formation of two distinct magnetic phases. arxiv-2505-05817.title: The Experience of Running: Recommending Routes Using Sensory Mapping in Urban Environments
arxiv-2505-05817.creator: Katrin Hänsel, Luca Maria Aiello, Daniele Quercia, Rossano Schifanella, Krisztian Zsolt Varga, Linus W. Dietz, Marios Constantinides
arxiv-2505-05817.description: Abstract Depending on the route, runners may experience frustration, freedom, or fulfilment. However, finding routes that are conducive to the psychological experience of running remains an unresolved task in the literature. In a mixed-method study, we interviewed 7 runners to identify themes contributing to running experience, and quantitatively examined these themes in an online survey with 387 runners.

arxiv-2510-00311.title: CORTEX: Collaborative LLM Agents for High-Stakes Alert Triage
arxiv-2510-00311.creator: Bowen Wei, Yuan Shen Tay, Howard Liu, Jinhao Pan, Kun Luo, Ziwei Zhu, Chris Jordan
arxiv-2510-00311.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bowen Wei, Yuan Shen Tay, Howard Liu, Jinhao Pan, Kun Luo, Ziwei Zhu, Chris Jordan. Security Operations Centers (SOCs) are overwhelmed by tens of thousands of daily alerts, of which only a small fraction correspond to genuine attacks. This overload creates alert fatigue, leading to overlooked threats and analyst burnout.

arxiv-2510-08786.title: The p p -adic distance of special points to subvarieties Thanks: The author was supported by the Marsden Fund administered by the Royal Society of New Zealand. He also thanks the Clay Foundation for partially supporting his attendance to the Tate Centennial Conference.
arxiv-2510-08786.creator: José Felipe Voloch
arxiv-2510-08786.description: Abstract . In a paper of Tate and the author, we conjectured a uniform bound for the p p -adic distance of torsion points on a semiabelian variety, not lying in a subvariety, to that subvariety. We survey the progress made on that conjecture and on similar statements in analogous situations. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 14G20, 11G25 1.

pmc-11327066.title: Natural herbal extract roles and mechanisms in treating cerebral ischemia: A systematic review
pmc-11327066.creator: Jiashuo Yang, Bo Yu, Jian Zheng
pmc-11327066.description: BackgroundStroke has been the focus of medical research due to its serious consequences and sequelae. Among the tens of millions of new stroke patients every year, cerebral ischemia patients account for the vast majority. While cerebral ischemia drug research and development is still ongoing, most drugs are terminated at preclinical stages due to their unacceptable toxic side effects.

pmc-11345448.title: Paving the way for affordable and equitable liposomal amphotericin B access worldwide
pmc-11345448.creator: Janice Soo Fern Lee, Rachel M Cohen, Rahela Ambaras Khan, Jessica Burry, Esther C Casas, Han Yang Chung, Luiz Henrique Costa, Nathan Ford, Diogo Lopes Nunes Galvao, Nora Giron, Joseph N Jarvis, Mousumi Mondal, Justine Jelagat Odionyi, Carmen Pérez Casas, Ajay Rangaraj, Joelle Rode, Carol Ruffell, Om
pmc-11345448.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryAmphotericin B has long been crucial for treating many serious infectious diseases, such as invasive fungal infections and visceral leishmaniasis, particularly for patients who are immunocompromised, including those with advanced HIV infection. The conventional amphotericin B deoxycholate formulation has largely been replaced in high-income countries with liposomal amphotericin B (LAmB), which has many advantages, including lower rates of adverse events, such as nephrotoxicity and anaemia.

pmc-11432201.title: Advanced Prediction of Hepatic Oncogenic Transformation in HBV Patients via RNA-Seq Data Analysis and Deep Learning Techniques
pmc-11432201.creator: Zhengtai Li, Lei Huang, Changyuan Yu
pmc-11432201.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Liver cancer, recognized as a significant global health issue, is increasingly correlated with Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, as evidenced by numerous scientific studies. This study aims to examine the correlation between HBV infection and the development of liver cancer, focusing on using RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to detect HBV sequences and applying deep learning techniques to estimate the likelihood of oncogenic transformation in individuals with HBV.

pmc-12786169.title: Digitally Enabled Discharge Quality After Neurosurgical Traumatic Brain Injury: A 10-Year Cohort from a Brazilian Public Tertiary Center
pmc-12786169.creator: Roberto Salvador Souza Guimarães, Victoria Ragognete Guimarães, Carlos Marcelo Barros, Maísa Ribeiro Pereira Lima Brigagão, Francisca Rego
pmc-12786169.description: Highlights What are the main findings? In a 10-year cohort of 559 neursurgical TBI discharges at a Brazilian public tertiary center, warning sign counseling was documented in 16.1% (95% CI 13.2–19.5) and palliative care referrals were 0%.EHR documentation exposed specific, digitally fixable gaps in the discharge process that can be measured as process quality indicators.

pmc-13445937.title: Sagittal alignment patterns in forward head posture: an EOS-based head-to-pelvis correlation analysis
pmc-13445937.creator: Katterine N. Rios-Peralta, Ali Firouzabadi, Kathleen M. Curran, David B. MacManus, Lukas Schönnagel, Matthias Pumberger, Hendrik Schmidt
pmc-13445937.description: Study DesignRetrospective radiographic study.ObjectivesForward head posture (FHP) is commonly observed in individuals with prolonged screen exposure and may affect spinal alignment. Because the craniovertebral angle (CVA) alone does not fully capture how sagittal balance is distributed across the spine, this study evaluated head-to-pelvis sagittal alignment patterns in individuals with and without FHP, with particular attention to the upper cervical region.
